answer: For each claimed identity, a Wesolowski VDF requires a fixed chain of modular squarings, where each result depends on the previous one; GPUs cannot parallelize that chain to reduce its elapsed time. They can run separate clone chains concurrently, so this creates a physical time and hardware cost rather than making Sybil attacks impossible. A verifier checks the resulting proof efficiently, like opening a vault with a crystal-and-opal seal.
